intent.raw_query: Japan family with kids, $4500, cherry blossom season 2026, 10 days from NYC

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience the iconic Japanese tradition of hanami (flower viewing) beneath hundreds of cherry blossom trees, including the famous weeping cherry tree illuminated at night. Pack a picnic, join locals in celebrating the season, and capture stunning photos of pink blooms reflected in the park's pond. A quintessential family-friendly cultural experience.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise Shopping Street
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple, dating back to 628 AD. Walk through the Thunder Gate (Kaminarimon) and explore the vibrant Nakamise shopping street lined with traditional snacks and souvenirs. Kids will love the festive atmosphere, fortune-telling slips (omikuji), and street food like ningyo-yaki (character-shaped cakes).

experiences.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park
experiences.description: A deeply moving and historically significant experience for older children and adults. Tour the Peace Memorial Museum to understand the events of 1945, walk through the Peace Memorial Park, and see the iconic A-Bomb Dome. This experience fosters reflection, empathy, and historical awareness, making it one of the most impactful cultural visits in Japan.

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park
experiences.description: Stroll through the ethereal bamboo forest of Arashiyama, one of Japan's most photographed landscapes, especially magical during cherry blossom season. Afterward, hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park where over 120 wild Japanese macaques roam freely — a thrilling family activity with panoramic views of Kyoto. Combine with a rickshaw ride for extra fun.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Japanese culinary culture at the legendary Tsukiji Outer Market, still buzzing with fresh seafood, tamagoyaki (sweet egg omelette), matcha treats, and street snacks. Join a guided family-friendly food tour to sample sushi, grilled scallops, fresh tuna, and traditional Japanese breakfast items. An immersive, delicious way to connect with local food culture and daily life.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Narita/Haneda Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, pick up a prepaid IC card (Suica or Pasmo) and pocket Wi-Fi at the airport. Take the airport limousine bus or train to your accommodation (Aegean Bliss Resort). Grab a quick convenience store meal from 7-Eleven or FamilyMart near the hotel — onigiri, sandwiches, and hot foods are cheap and delicious.

meals.breakfast: N/A (in-flight)
meals.lunch: N/A (in-flight)
meals.dinner: Convenience store (7-Eleven / FamilyMart) near hotel — budget ¥600–¥900 per person

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is purely arrival. Rest well — you have a full 9 days ahead. Purchase your IC card at the airport to make all train and bus travel seamless. A JR Pass may be worth buying in advance if you plan to travel between Tokyo, Kyoto, and Hiroshima.

day_by_day.morning: Recover from jet lag with a slow morning. Walk around the immediate hotel neighborhood to get oriented. Visit a local konbini for a cheap Japanese breakfast — onigiri, tamagoyaki, and green tea. Head to the nearest local shrine or park for a gentle introduction to Japanese culture and enjoy any early cherry blossom sightings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a nearby covered shopping arcade (shotengai) for budget souvenirs and snacks. Try a local ramen or udon shop for lunch. Visit a 100-yen shop (Daiso or Seria) to stock up on travel essentials and affordable Japanese goods.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the beachfront near your hotel at sunset. Have dinner at a nearby izakaya (Japanese pub) — order yakitori skewers, edamame, and karaage chicken. These are affordable and quintessentially Japanese.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store breakfast — ¥400–¥600 per person
meals.lunch: Local ramen or udon shop — ¥700–¥1,000 per person
meals.dinner: Neighborhood izakaya — ¥1,200–¥1,800 per person

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 2 light to adjust to the time difference. Japan is typically UTC+9. Avoid overscheduling on your first full day. Cherry blossoms in mid-April may still be in bloom depending on the region — check local bloom forecasts.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Tokyo (if not already based there). Head to Senso-ji Temple in Asakusa — Tokyo's oldest Buddhist temple dating to 628 AD. Arrive early (by 8:00–9:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Walk through the iconic Kaminarimon (Thunder Gate) and explore the temple grounds. Entry to the temple is FREE.
day_by_day.afternoon: Browse Nakamise Shopping Street just outside Senso-ji for affordable traditional snacks (ningyo-yaki, senbei rice crackers) and budget souvenirs. Walk to nearby Ueno Park — one of Tokyo's best cherry blossom spots — for a hanami picnic. Buy picnic supplies from a convenience store or the Ameyoko market stalls.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Akihabara (Electric Town) for a fun, uniquely Japanese evening experience. Window-shop anime, electronics, and arcades. Have dinner at a budget conveyor-belt sushi restaurant (kaiten-zushi) such as Sushiro or Kura Sushi — plates start at ¥110.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or hotel — ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Convenience store picnic in Ueno Park — ¥600–¥900
meals.dinner: Kaiten-zushi (conveyor belt sushi) — ¥1,000–¥1,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free to enter. Ueno Park is free. Nakamise Shopping Street is great for budget omiyage (souvenir) shopping. Use your IC card for all train travel in Tokyo — it's the cheapest and most convenient option.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden — one of Japan's most beautiful parks and a premier cherry blossom viewing location. Entry is only ¥500 per adult (children under 15 are free). Spend the morning doing hanami under the sakura trees. Bring snacks from a convenience store for a picnic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Harajuku and walk down Takeshita Street — a colorful, quirky pedestrian shopping street popular with families. Try a crepe from one of the street stalls (¥400–¥600). Walk through Yoyogi Park, which is free and often has street performers and cherry blossoms. Visit the Meiji Jingu Shrine nearby — free entry, beautiful forested grounds.
day_by_day.evening: Take the train to Shibuya to witness the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing — one of the busiest intersections in the world. Watch from the free observation area at Mag's Park or Starbucks overlooking the crossing. Have dinner at a yoshoku (Western-influenced Japanese) restaurant or a gyudon (beef bowl) chain like Yoshinoya or Sukiya — budget-friendly and filling.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store — ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Picnic in Shinjuku Gyoen / Harajuku crepe — ¥500–¥800
meals.dinner: Gyudon chain restaurant (Yoshinoya/Sukiya) — ¥500–¥800 per person

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen entry: ¥500 adults, free for under 15. Meiji Jingu and Yoyogi Park are both free. Mid-April cherry blossoms should still be lovely. Shibuya Scramble is best experienced in the evening when it's most dramatic.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Shinkansen (bullet train) from Tokyo to Kyoto — approximately 2 hours 15 minutes using the JR Pass or purchasing a ticket (¥13,320 one way without JR Pass). Arrive in Kyoto and check in to a budget guesthouse or capsule hotel. Head to Fushimi Inari Taisha Shrine — famous for thousands of vermillion torii gates. Entry is FREE and it opens 24 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the torii gate trail up the mountain — the full hike takes 2–3 hours but you can turn back at any point for great views and photos. Descend and take a short train ride to the Nishiki Market ('Kyoto's Kitchen') — a narrow covered market with free food samples and affordable street food like tamagoyaki and pickled vegetables.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the Gion district at dusk — Kyoto's famous geisha quarter. Walk along Hanamikoji Street and Shirakawa Canal for beautiful traditional architecture and possible geisha sightings. Have dinner at a budget teishoku (set meal) restaurant near Gion — look for places with plastic food displays outside showing prices.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store on the Shinkansen or at Tokyo Station — ¥500–¥700
meals.lunch: Nishiki Market street food — ¥700–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Teishoku set meal restaurant in Gion area — ¥900–¥1,400

day_by_day.notes: Fushimi Inari is completely free and one of Japan's most iconic sights. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the torii gate hike. The JR Pass covers the Shinkansen between Tokyo and Kyoto and may be cost-effective if purchased in advance. Gion strolling is free.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Arashiyama Bamboo Grove early in the morning (before 8:00 AM) to avoid crowds. Entry to the grove is FREE. Walk through the towering bamboo stalks and continue to Tenryu-ji Temple garden (¥500 garden entry, temple interior extra). Explore the scenic Togetsukyo Bridge and the Oi River area — beautiful with spring foliage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short bus ride to Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion) — Kyoto's most famous landmark. Entry is ¥500 per person. The gold-leaf covered pavilion reflecting in the pond is stunning. Continue to Ryoan-ji Temple (¥600) to see Japan's most famous Zen rock garden — a wonderful cultural and contemplative experience for all ages.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Kyoto. Visit Pontocho Alley — a narrow lantern-lit dining street along the Kamo River. Look for affordable set menus posted outside restaurants. Alternatively, grab dinner at a standing soba or ramen bar for an authentic and budget-friendly experience. End the evening with a walk along the Kamo River.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or guesthouse breakfast — ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Arashiyama area tofu cuisine set lunch or bento — ¥900–¥1,300
meals.dinner: Pontocho standing ramen or soba bar — ¥700–¥1,200

day_by_day.notes: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove is free but very crowded after 9 AM — go early! Kinkaku-ji (¥500) and Ryoan-ji (¥600) are both worth the entry fees. Use Kyoto city buses with a ¥600 day pass for unlimited rides — very economical for temple-hopping.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Philosopher's Path (Tetsugaku no Michi) — a scenic stone path along a canal lined with cherry trees. One of Kyoto's most beloved hanami spots and completely FREE. Walk the 2 km path from Nanzen-ji to Ginkaku-ji (Silver Pavilion). Visit Nanzen-ji Temple complex — free to enter the grounds, with optional paid inner sanctuaries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Ginkaku-ji (Silver Pavilion) at the northern end of Philosopher's Path — entry ¥500. Explore the beautiful sand garden and moss garden. Take a bus to Nijo Castle (¥800 entry) — a UNESCO World Heritage Site with stunning Edo-period architecture, 'nightingale floors,' and beautiful spring gardens. Great for history-loving families.
day_by_day.afternoon_note: Nijo Castle is excellent for children due to the squeaky nightingale floors designed to detect intruders.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local sento (public bathhouse) for a traditional Japanese bathing experience — typically ¥450–¥500 per person. This is a wonderful cultural activity for families (separate male/female sections). Afterward, have dinner at a budget karaage or tonkatsu restaurant near your accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store — ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Bento box from a supermarket near Philosopher's Path — ¥600–¥900
meals.dinner: Tonkatsu or karaage restaurant — ¥900–¥1,300

day_by_day.notes: Philosopher's Path is free and magical in cherry blossom season. Mid-April should still have late blooms. Nijo Castle (¥800) is excellent for history enthusiasts and families. The sento experience is a uniquely Japanese cultural activity — bring a small towel or rent one for ¥50–¥100.

day_by_day.morning: Take the JR train from Kyoto to Hiroshima (approximately 1.5 hours by Shinkansen, covered by JR Pass). Head directly to the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum — one of the most historically significant and moving museums in the world. Entry is only ¥200 per adult (children free). Allow 2–3 hours for the museum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park — free to enter. Visit the A-Bomb Dome (Genbaku Dome), a UNESCO World Heritage Site preserved as a reminder of the atomic bombing. Pay respects at the Children's Peace Monument and the Flame of Peace. Take a short ferry to Miyajima Island (¥180 JR ferry, covered by JR Pass) — famous for the 'floating' Otorii Gate of Itsukushima Shrine.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Miyajima Island — walk around the shrine area (free outer grounds, ¥300 for inner shrine), meet the friendly wild deer, and enjoy the scenic mountain backdrop. Return to Hiroshima by ferry. Have dinner at a local okonomiyaki restaurant — Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki (layered savory pancake) is a must-try local specialty and very budget-friendly.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store at Kyoto Station before departure — ¥500–¥700
meals.lunch: Picnic in Peace Memorial Park or onigiri from a konbini — ¥500–¥800
meals.dinner: Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki restaurant — ¥900–¥1,300

day_by_day.notes: The Peace Memorial Museum (¥200) is deeply moving and suitable for older children and teens — it may be intense for very young children. The museum provides important historical context. Miyajima's famous floating torii gate is best seen at high tide. Check tide times in advance. JR Pass covers the ferry to Miyajima.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the Tokyo/coastal area or explore Osaka as a day trip from Hiroshima or Kyoto (Osaka is 15 minutes from Kyoto by Shinkansen). Visit Osaka Castle (¥600 museum entry, grounds are free) — a magnificent reconstructed castle with panoramic city views and excellent historical exhibits about the Sengoku period. Great for history-loving families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Dotonbori — Osaka's famous entertainment and food district. Walk along the canal and take photos with the iconic Glico Running Man sign. Try Osaka's famous street foods: takoyaki (octopus balls, ¥500–¥600 for 8 pieces), taiyaki (fish-shaped pastry), and kushikatsu (deep-fried skewers). Dotonbori is free to walk around.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Shinsaibashi shopping arcade for window shopping and people-watching. Visit the free observation deck at Umeda Sky Building for panoramic Osaka views (or save the ¥1,500 entry for another experience). Have a final Osaka dinner — try a budget conveyor-belt sushi or a filling ramen shop. Return to your accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Hotel/guesthouse or convenience store — ¥400–¥700
meals.lunch: Dotonbori street food (takoyaki, taiyaki, kushikatsu) — ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Ramen shop or kaiten-zushi in Osaka/Kyoto — ¥900–¥1,400

day_by_day.notes: Osaka is extremely easy to reach from Kyoto (15 min by Shinkansen or 30 min by regular express train). Dotonbori is one of Japan's most vibrant areas and completely free to explore. Osaka is known as 'Japan's kitchen' — food is exceptional and affordable. Keep receipts for any tax-free shopping.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — revisit your favorite local area near the hotel for a peaceful last walk. If near a park, do one final cherry blossom viewing (hanami) session. Visit a local morning market or farmers' market if available. Buy any last-minute omiyage (souvenirs) from a 100-yen shop or local sweet shop — wagashi (traditional sweets) make excellent gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearest major train station or airport for your departure. Allow plenty of travel time — at least 2–3 hours before your flight. Use remaining IC card balance on snacks and drinks at the airport. Return any rented pocket Wi-Fi devices at the airport. Exchange or use remaining yen at the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Reflect on 10 incredible days of cherry blossoms, culture, history, and family memories across Japan!

meals.breakfast: Hotel or local café — ¥500–¥800
meals.lunch: Airport terminal food (ekiben bento box is excellent and affordable) — ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: In-flight or airport restaurant

day_by_day.notes: Return your IC card at the airport for a ¥500 deposit refund (minus a small handling fee). Return pocket Wi-Fi at the airport rental counter. Japan has strict rules about bringing food items home — declare anything at customs. Keep your JR Pass and transport cards until you've completed all journeys. Tax-free purchases require your passport at checkout.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at airport, clear customs and immigration, collect luggage. Take the airport limousine bus or train to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest to beat jet lag.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at a 24-hour convenience store (7-Eleven, Lawson, or FamilyMart) near the hotel — try onigiri, sandwiches, and warm ramen cups for an authentic and affordable late-night Japanese experience (¥500–¥1,000)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Purchase a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport for easy transit throughout your trip. Exchange some yen at the airport for convenience. Estimated taxi/bus to resort: ¥1,500–¥3,500 depending on location.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in to recover from jet lag. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Take a slow morning walk along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort to soak in the surroundings and orient yourselves to the area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearest local neighborhood — visit a nearby shrine or temple for a gentle cultural introduction. Browse local shops and pick up any essentials. If the resort is near a city center, take a short walk to a local market or covered shopping arcade.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed dinner near the hotel. Explore the waterfront or resort area as the sun sets. Early bedtime to continue adjusting to Japan Standard Time.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast buffet or a nearby kissaten (Japanese coffee shop) — enjoy toast, eggs, and coffee for ¥600–¥1,200
meals.lunch: Local ramen or udon shop near the hotel — hearty and affordable at ¥800–¥1,500 per person
meals.dinner: Mid-range family restaurant (Gusto, Denny's Japan, or a local izakaya) near the resort — ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: This is an intentional recovery and orientation day. Don't over-schedule — jet lag can be especially tough for families with children. Stay hydrated and avoid heavy activity.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise Shopping Street in Asakusa, Tokyo. Arrive early (by 8:00–9:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Walk through the iconic Kaminarimon (Thunder Gate), stroll Nakamise-dori lined with traditional snacks and souvenirs, and explore the temple grounds. Light incense and try omikuji (fortune slips) for a cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the temple, walk along the Sumida River waterfront. Visit the nearby Tokyo Skytree for panoramic city views (tickets ¥2,100 adults, ¥1,550 children) — a great family activity. Browse the Solamachi shopping complex at the base of Skytree for souvenirs and snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Asakusa area for dinner. Take a leisurely stroll along Nakamise again in the evening when it's less crowded and beautifully lit.

meals.breakfast: Grab a fresh ningyo-yaki (small sponge cakes) or melonpan from a Nakamise vendor as a morning snack — ¥200–¥500
meals.lunch: Tempura don or soba at a traditional restaurant near Senso-ji — ¥1,000–¥1,800 per person
meals.dinner: Monjayaki or okonomiyaki restaurant in Asakusa — fun, interactive dining perfect for families at ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free to enter. Wear comfortable walking shoes. Nakamise shops typically open around 10:00 AM. The Tokyo Skytree Tembo Deck requires timed tickets — book online in advance to avoid queues.

day_by_day.morning: Cherry Blossom Viewing at a top Tokyo hanami spot — head to Ueno Park or Shinjuku Gyoen (entry ¥500 adults, ¥250 children). Mid-April is the tail end of Tokyo's cherry blossom season, so blossoms may be late-stage but still beautiful. Bring a picnic blanket and enjoy hanami (flower viewing) like a local family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Ueno Zoo (adjacent to Ueno Park) — Japan's oldest zoo, home to giant pandas and beloved by families (¥600 adults, ¥200 children). Alternatively, explore the Tokyo National Museum in Ueno for a deep dive into Japanese history and art (¥1,000 adults, free for children under 18).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Akihabara for a fun family evening — explore the multi-story electronics shops, anime stores, and vibrant neon-lit streets. Visit a themed café or arcade for a uniquely Japanese experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or convenience store picnic items to bring to the park — onigiri, sandwiches, and juice (¥500–¥1,000)
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch under the cherry blossoms in the park — pick up bento boxes from a nearby convenience store or supermarket (¥600–¥1,200 per person)
meals.dinner: Akihabara ramen shop or a curry house — try Japanese curry rice, a family favorite at ¥1,000–¥1,800 per person

day_by_day.notes: April 18 may still have some cherry blossoms depending on the year — check bloom forecasts closer to the date. Shinjuku Gyoen prohibits alcohol, making it a great family-friendly hanami spot. Ueno Park is more festive and lively.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Shinkansen (bullet train) from Tokyo to Kyoto — approximately 2 hours 15 minutes on the Nozomi or Hikari line (¥13,000–¥14,000 per person, covered by JR Pass if purchased). Arrive in Kyoto mid-morning. Check into your Kyoto accommodation or store luggage and begin exploring.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Arashiyama Bamboo Grove — stroll through the iconic towering bamboo forest, one of Japan's most photographed landscapes. Afterward, hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park (entry ¥550 adults, ¥250 children) for spectacular views of Kyoto and close-up encounters with wild Japanese macaques — a huge hit with families.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the charming Arashiyama riverside area. Rent a rowboat on the Oi River, browse local craft shops, or enjoy a quiet walk along the Togetsukyo Bridge at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick stop at Tokyo Station's famous ekiben (station bento) shops before boarding the Shinkansen — ¥800–¥1,500
meals.lunch: Tofu kaiseki or yudofu (tofu hot pot) at a traditional Arashiyama restaurant — Kyoto is famous for its tofu cuisine at ¥1,500–¥2,500 per person
meals.dinner: Riverside restaurant in Arashiyama or a casual izakaya in central Kyoto — ¥2,000–¥3,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Arashiyama Bamboo Grove is best visited early morning or late afternoon to avoid peak crowds. The Monkey Park involves a 20-minute uphill hike — wear comfortable shoes. If traveling with young children, the hike is manageable but bring water.

day_by_day.morning: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park, Kyoto — experience the iconic Japanese tradition of hanami beneath hundreds of cherry blossoms. The park's famous weeping cherry tree (shidarezakura) is breathtaking. Arrive early for a peaceful experience before crowds arrive. The park is free to enter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the adjacent Yasaka Shrine and the historic Gion district — wander the atmospheric stone-paved lanes of Hanamikoji Street where you may spot geiko (Kyoto geisha) heading to appointments. Visit Kiyomizudera Temple (entry ¥500) perched on a hillside with stunning city views — a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the Higashiyama district's preserved machiya (townhouse) streets, beautifully lit in the evening. Enjoy a traditional Kyoto dinner.

meals.breakfast: Japanese breakfast set at a local kissaten or hotel — miso soup, rice, grilled fish, pickles (¥800–¥1,500)
meals.lunch: Nishin soba (herring soba noodles) — a Kyoto specialty — at a noodle shop near Maruyama Park (¥1,000–¥1,500 per person)
meals.dinner: Obanzai cuisine (Kyoto-style small dishes) at a mid-range restaurant in Gion — ¥2,000–¥3,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Maruyama Park is free and open 24 hours. Kiyomizudera can be crowded — visit before 9:00 AM if possible. The walk between Maruyama Park, Yasaka Shrine, and Kiyomizudera is entirely walkable and very scenic. Comfortable shoes are essential.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Fushimi Inari Taisha — the iconic shrine famous for thousands of vermillion torii gates winding up a forested mountain. The shrine is free and open 24 hours. Walk as far as you like — even the first 30 minutes of the trail offers spectacular photo opportunities. A great outdoor activity for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel to Nishiki Market — Kyoto's famous covered market street known as 'Kyoto's Kitchen.' Sample local foods including pickled vegetables, fresh tofu, skewered seafood, and sweet mochi. Browse the stalls and interact with local vendors for an authentic cultural experience.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Philosopher's Path (Tetsugaku-no-Michi) — a peaceful stone canal path lined with cherry trees (late blossoms possible in mid-April). End the evening at a cozy neighborhood restaurant near your hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early convenience store breakfast before heading to Fushimi Inari — ¥500–¥800
meals.lunch: Street food and tastings at Nishiki Market — budget ¥1,000–¥2,000 per person for a satisfying market lunch
meals.dinner: Shabu-shabu (hot pot) restaurant in central Kyoto — interactive and family-friendly dining at ¥2,500–¥3,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Fushimi Inari is best visited at opening (early morning) or late afternoon to avoid tour groups. The full hike to the summit takes 2–3 hours but families can turn back at any point. Nishiki Market stalls typically open from 10:00 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Travel by Shinkansen from Kyoto to Hiroshima — approximately 1 hour 20 minutes (¥5,500–¥6,000 per person, JR Pass eligible). Upon arrival, head directly to the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park. Tour the museum's deeply moving exhibits documenting the 1945 atomic bombing — appropriate for older children and adults. Visit the iconic A-Bomb Dome (Genbaku Dome), a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Hiroshima Peace Memorial Park — visit the Children's Peace Monument (Sadako's statue) and fold origami cranes as a family tribute. Take a short ferry to Miyajima Island (Itsukushima) — home to the famous floating torii gate of Itsukushima Shrine. Spot the friendly wild deer roaming freely around the island.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hiroshima city. Enjoy a relaxed evening in the Hondori shopping arcade area.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or grab onigiri and coffee at Kyoto Station before boarding the Shinkansen — ¥500–¥1,000
meals.lunch: Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki (savory pancake with noodles) — a must-try local specialty at Okonomimura (Okonomiyaki Village) — ¥1,000–¥1,500 per person
meals.dinner: Oysters — Hiroshima is Japan's top oyster producer. Try grilled or fried oysters at a local seafood restaurant — ¥2,000–¥3,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Peace Memorial Museum entry is ¥200 for adults, free for children. Allow at least 2 hours for the museum. The Miyajima ferry costs approximately ¥180 each way (JR Pass holders ride free). The floating torii is best seen at high tide — check tide times in advance. This is an emotionally heavy day — be prepared to discuss history sensitively with children.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Shinkansen back toward Tokyo, stopping in Osaka for a day of exploration. Arrive in Osaka mid-morning. Visit Osaka Castle (Osaka-jo) — a magnificent 16th-century fortress surrounded by beautiful gardens (entry ¥600 adults, free for children under 15). The castle grounds are a lovely spot for a final cherry blossom viewing if late blooms remain.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Dotonbori — Osaka's vibrant entertainment and food district. Walk along the famous canal, see the iconic Glico Running Man sign, and browse the lively streets. Visit the nearby Shinsaibashi shopping arcade for souvenirs. Try takoyaki (octopus balls) fresh from a street stall — a quintessential Osaka experience.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Osaka's legendary food scene — known as 'Japan's Kitchen' (kuidaore). Explore more of Dotonbori's neon-lit streets before boarding the Shinkansen back to Tokyo or your resort area.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Shinkansen ekiben — ¥800–¥1,500
meals.lunch: Osaka street food crawl in Dotonbori — takoyaki (¥500), kushikatsu (¥800), and taiyaki (¥200) — budget ¥1,500–¥2,000 per person
meals.dinner: Kani Doraku or a mid-range restaurant in Dotonbori for fresh crab or Osaka-style teppanyaki — ¥2,500–¥3,500 per person

day_by_day.notes: Osaka Castle's main tower museum is optional — the exterior and grounds alone are worth the visit and free to walk around. Dotonbori is very crowded in the evening — keep an eye on children. The Shinkansen back from Osaka to Tokyo runs frequently — book seats in advance during peak travel season.

day_by_day.morning: Return to the resort area. Spend a final leisurely morning at Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy the beachfront, have a long breakfast, and soak in the last moments of your Japan trip. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: If time allows before checkout, visit a nearby local attraction — a final temple, scenic viewpoint, or local market. Pick up any last-minute omiyage (souvenir gifts) for friends and family back home at a local shop or convenience store.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to the airport for departure. Arrive at least 2–3 hours before your flight. Enjoy a final Japanese meal at the airport — many Japanese airports have excellent food courts with regional specialties.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — savor it! Or visit a local café for a Japanese morning set (¥800–¥1,500)
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the hotel or at the airport — try a tonkatsu (breaded pork cutlet) set meal (¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Airport dining — explore the terminal food options for a final taste of Japan (¥1,500–¥2,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Allow extra time for airport transit. Confirm your flight details and check-in requirements. Return your Suica/Pasmo card at the airport for a refund of the deposit (¥500). Duty-free shopping is available at most Japanese international airports. Don't forget to declare any items over your home country's customs allowance.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Cherry Blossom Viewing in Maruyama Park
experiences.description: Experience the iconic Japanese tradition of hanami (flower viewing) beneath hundreds of cherry blossom trees, including the famous weeping cherry tree illuminated at night. Pack a picnic, join locals in celebrating the season, and capture stunning photos of pink blooms reflected in the park's pond. A quintessential family-friendly cultural experience.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise Shopping Street
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple, dating back to 628 AD. Walk through the Thunder Gate (Kaminarimon) and explore the vibrant Nakamise shopping street lined with traditional snacks and souvenirs. Kids will love the festive atmosphere, fortune-telling slips (omikuji), and street food like ningyo-yaki (character-shaped cakes).

experiences.name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park
experiences.description: A deeply moving and historically significant experience for older children and adults. Tour the Peace Memorial Museum to understand the events of 1945, walk through the Peace Memorial Park, and see the iconic A-Bomb Dome. This experience fosters reflection, empathy, and historical awareness, making it one of the most impactful cultural visits in Japan.

experiences.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and Monkey Park
experiences.description: Stroll through the ethereal bamboo forest of Arashiyama, one of Japan's most photographed landscapes, especially magical during cherry blossom season. Afterward, hike up to Iwatayama Monkey Park where over 120 wild Japanese macaques roam freely — a thrilling family activity with panoramic views of Kyoto. Combine with a rickshaw ride for extra fun.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Japanese culinary culture at the legendary Tsukiji Outer Market, still buzzing with fresh seafood, tamagoyaki (sweet egg omelette), matcha treats, and street snacks. Join a guided family-friendly food tour to sample sushi, grilled scallops, fresh tuna, and traditional Japanese breakfast items. An immersive, delicious way to connect with local food culture and daily life.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Narita/Haneda Airport on Flight UA at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, then arrange a pre-booked luxury private transfer (Mercedes V-Class or similar) to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome amenity prepared by the resort.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Late-night in-room dining at the resort — request a curated Japanese welcome platter with seasonal sashimi, miso soup, and premium sake to ease into Japanese cuisine after a long flight

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange airport meet-and-greet service and a dedicated porter for luggage. Confirm resort check-in is prepared for late arrival. Keep Day 1 light — rest is the priority to combat jet lag.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely resort breakfast. Take a gentle orientation walk along the beachfront property to acclimate to the surroundings. Arrange a private concierge briefing to confirm all upcoming reservations and transport logistics for the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local coastal area near the resort. Visit a nearby Shinto shrine for a calm, culturally immersive introduction to Japanese spiritual traditions. Many coastal towns feature beautifully preserved shrines with ocean backdrops — a serene way to begin the cultural journey.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a private kaiseki dinner at the resort's signature restaurant. Kaiseki is Japan's most refined multi-course culinary tradition, featuring seasonal ingredients presented as edible art. Pair with a curated sake flight selected by the sommelier.

meals.breakfast: Full Japanese breakfast at the resort — grilled fish, tamagoyaki (rolled omelette), miso soup, pickled vegetables, and steamed rice, plus Western options
meals.lunch: Light beachside lunch at the resort — fresh seafood donburi (rice bowl) and cold matcha
meals.dinner: Private kaiseki dinner at the resort's fine dining restaurant — 10-course seasonal menu with sake pairing

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to recover from travel and get oriented. Ask the concierge to book any remaining restaurant reservations — top Japanese restaurants require weeks of advance booking. April is peak cherry blossom season, so parks will be lively and beautiful.

day_by_day.morning: Depart by private luxury vehicle or Shinkansen (bullet train) toward Kyoto. Arrive in Kyoto and head directly to Maruyama Park for a premium Cherry Blossom Viewing (Hanami) experience. In April, the iconic weeping cherry tree at the park's center is typically in full bloom. Hire a private cultural guide to explain the history and meaning of hanami traditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Kyoto's Higashiyama district on foot — stroll the stone-paved Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka lanes lined with traditional machiya townhouses, artisan shops, and tea houses. Visit Kiyomizudera Temple perched dramatically on the hillside for panoramic city views.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a private tea ceremony in a historic Kyoto machiya (townhouse) arranged exclusively for your group. Afterward, dine at a renowned Kyoto kaiseki restaurant in the Gion district.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure — Japanese set with seasonal grilled fish and pickles
meals.lunch: Lunch at a high-end tofu cuisine restaurant in Kyoto (yudofu — silken tofu hot pot) near Nanzenji Temple
meals.dinner: Kaiseki dinner at a Michelin-starred Gion restaurant — reserve Kikunoi Honten or Nakamura for an authentic Kyoto fine dining experience

day_by_day.notes: Maruyama Park is best visited in the morning before crowds peak. Wear comfortable walking shoes for Higashiyama. A private guide for Kyoto is highly recommended to unlock hidden cultural context. Book the tea ceremony well in advance through the concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a private guided visit to Arashiyama. Walk through the ethereal Arashiyama Bamboo Grove at dawn before the crowds arrive — the morning light filtering through towering bamboo stalks is otherworldly. Continue to the Arashiyama Monkey Park (Iwatayama) for a family-friendly adventure — hike up the hillside to interact with Japanese macaques with sweeping views of Kyoto below.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Tenryuji Temple and its UNESCO-listed garden, one of Kyoto's finest Zen gardens with a backdrop of Arashiyama mountains. Take a private boat ride along the Oi River for a scenic, relaxed afternoon. Visit the Okochi Sanso Villa garden for a tranquil stroll and matcha tea.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kyoto city center. Stroll through Gion in the early evening — if fortunate, spot a geiko (geisha) or maiko (apprentice geisha) heading to an engagement. Enjoy a private dinner in a traditional Gion ochaya (teahouse) setting.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel or a traditional Kyoto kissaten (coffee shop) near Arashiyama
meals.lunch: Riverside lunch at Arashiyama — fresh yuba (tofu skin) cuisine at Shigetsu restaurant within Tenryuji Temple complex
meals.dinner: Private multi-course dinner at a Gion ochaya or a reservation at Hyotei, one of Kyoto's most celebrated historic restaurants

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the Bamboo Grove by 7:00–7:30 AM for the best experience with minimal crowds. The Monkey Park involves a 20-minute uphill hike — suitable for most family members. Bring yen cash for smaller vendors in Arashiyama.

day_by_day.morning: Travel by Shinkansen from Kyoto to Hiroshima (approximately 1 hour 15 minutes on the Nozomi). Upon arrival, visit the Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum and Park — a deeply moving and historically significant experience. Tour the Peace Memorial Museum, walk through the park, and observe the Atomic Bomb Dome (Genbaku Dome), a UNESCO World Heritage Site. A private guide is strongly recommended to provide thoughtful historical context for all ages.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short ferry ride to Miyajima Island (Itsukushima) — one of Japan's most scenic locations. See the iconic floating torii gate of Itsukushima Shrine at high tide, a breathtaking cultural and natural landmark. Explore the shrine complex and the island's friendly resident deer. Browse artisan shops for Miyajima's famous wooden rice paddles (shamoji).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hiroshima city. Enjoy dinner featuring Hiroshima's local specialties. Return to resort or stay overnight in Hiroshima at a luxury hotel (The Strings by InterContinental Hiroshima recommended) if distance requires.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the Shinkansen or at Kyoto station — premium ekiben (station bento box) featuring local Kyoto ingredients
meals.lunch: Lunch on Miyajima Island — fresh grilled oysters (Hiroshima is famous for them) and momiji manju (maple leaf-shaped cakes) at a waterfront restaurant
meals.dinner: Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki (savory layered pancake) at Micchan or a refined kaiseki dinner at The Strings by InterContinental Hiroshima

day_by_day.notes: The Peace Memorial Museum is emotionally intense — prepare children with age-appropriate context beforehand. Check tide times for Miyajima to see the torii gate at high tide (most photogenic). The ferry to Miyajima is covered by the JR Pass. Allow at least 2.5 hours for the museum and park.

day_by_day.morning: Travel by Shinkansen to Tokyo (approximately 4 hours from Hiroshima, or 2 hours from Kyoto if returning first). Upon arrival, check into a luxury Tokyo hotel (The Peninsula Tokyo, Aman Tokyo, or Mandarin Oriental recommended) or arrange day use if returning to the resort. Begin the Tokyo exploration with a visit to Senso-ji Temple in Asakusa — Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple dating to 628 AD. Walk through the Kaminarimon (Thunder Gate) and the bustling Nakamise Shopping Street.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Asakusa further — visit the Asakusa Culture Tourist Information Center rooftop for panoramic views. Take a private rickshaw (jinrikisha) tour through Asakusa's traditional streets. Cross the Sumida River by water taxi to Odaiba or head to Ueno for a cultural museum visit (Tokyo National Museum houses Japan's finest collection of art and antiquities).
day_by_day.evening: Experience Tokyo from above with cocktails at a sky-high bar — the New York Bar at Park Hyatt Tokyo (famous from Lost in Translation) or the Andaz Tokyo rooftop bar offer stunning nighttime views. Follow with a premium sushi omakase dinner in Ginza.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the Shinkansen — premium ekiben or dining car service
meals.lunch: Traditional tempura lunch at Daikokuya Tempura in Asakusa, a historic restaurant serving since 1887
meals.dinner: Omakase sushi dinner at a Ginza sushi counter — reserve Sushi Saito, Sushi Yoshitake, or Sushi Sho for a world-class 20-course chef's selection experience

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is most atmospheric in the early morning or evening — plan accordingly. Nakamise Shopping Street is excellent for premium souvenirs including lacquerware, fans, and textiles. Book the omakase sushi counter months in advance — these are among the hardest reservations in the world to secure; use the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the day with a private guided Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour — even though the inner wholesale market moved to Toyosu, the Outer Market remains a vibrant hub of fresh seafood, street food, and culinary culture. Sample tamagoyaki (sweet rolled omelette), fresh uni (sea urchin), premium tuna, and Japanese pickles. Learn about Japanese food culture from an expert guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Hamarikyu Gardens — a stunning traditional Japanese garden adjacent to Tokyo Bay, featuring a historic teahouse on a tidal pond. Enjoy a ceremonial matcha and wagashi (traditional sweets) in this serene setting. Afterward, explore the upscale Ginza district for luxury shopping — visit the Ginza Six complex, Itoya stationery flagship, and international and Japanese luxury brands.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional performing arts experience — reserve seats for a Kabuki performance at the Kabukiza Theatre in Ginza (single-act tickets available for families). Follow with a teppanyaki dinner at a premium Ginza restaurant where skilled chefs perform tableside.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Tsukiji Outer Market itself — fresh sushi breakfast or oysters with sake at a market stall (a beloved Tokyo tradition)
meals.lunch: Refined lunch at a kaiseki restaurant in Ginza or a premium ramen experience at Ginza Noodles
meals.dinner: Teppanyaki dinner at Ukai-tei Ginza — premium Wagyu beef prepared tableside in an elegant setting

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Tsukiji by 8:00 AM for the best selection and freshest products. The Kabukiza Theatre offers English audio guides — highly recommended. Hamarikyu Gardens requires a small entry fee. Ginza is ideal for purchasing premium Japanese goods including ceramics, lacquerware, and cosmetics.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to a day trip to Nikko (approximately 2 hours from Tokyo by private car or the Tobu Nikko Limited Express). Nikko is a UNESCO World Heritage Site featuring the extraordinarily ornate Toshogu Shrine — the mausoleum of Tokugawa Ieyasu, the founder of the Edo shogunate. Explore the gilded shrine complex set amid towering cedar forests.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko — visit Rinnoji Temple, the Yomeimon Gate (Gate of Sunlight), and Shinkyo Bridge, a sacred vermillion bridge over the Daiya River. If the family enjoys nature, take a short drive to Kegon Falls, one of Japan's most spectacular waterfalls, and the shores of Lake Chuzenji.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by private luxury vehicle. Enjoy a relaxed evening — consider a traditional Japanese onsen (hot spring bath) experience at a high-end Tokyo ryokan or spa facility. Dine at a premium shabu-shabu restaurant for a communal, family-friendly dinner experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure — full Japanese or Western set
meals.lunch: Traditional yuba (tofu skin) cuisine lunch at a Nikko restaurant — this is a Nikko specialty developed by monks
meals.dinner: Premium shabu-shabu dinner at Seryna or Imahan in Tokyo — thinly sliced Wagyu beef cooked at the table in a delicate broth

day_by_day.notes: Nikko can be crowded on weekends — a weekday visit is preferable. Hire a private guide for Nikko to fully appreciate the complex iconography of Toshogu Shrine. The Yomeimon Gate is extraordinarily detailed — budget extra time here. Wear comfortable shoes for uneven stone paths.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Tokyo's Yanaka district — one of the city's best-preserved historic neighborhoods that survived WWII bombing. Wander through Yanaka Cemetery (famous for cherry blossoms lining its paths in April), browse independent artisan shops, and visit traditional temples and shrines in this atmospheric shitamachi (old town) area. A private guide adds tremendous value here.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the teamLab Borderless or teamLab Planets digital art museum — an immersive, boundary-pushing experience that delights visitors of all ages with interactive light and art installations. Book tickets well in advance as these sell out. Afterward, explore the trendy Omotesando district — Tokyo's most architecturally stunning shopping boulevard — for premium Japanese designers and international luxury brands.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at one of Tokyo's most celebrated restaurants. Consider a reservation at Sukiyabashi Jiro (Honten or Roppongi branch) for legendary sushi, or opt for a stunning view dinner at the Mandarin Oriental or Conrad Tokyo's fine dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — enjoy a final leisurely morning meal
meals.lunch: Casual lunch in Yanaka — visit a traditional kissaten (old-school coffee shop) and try homemade curry or a local shokudo (neighborhood restaurant)
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner — Sukiyabashi Jiro Roppongi, or a Michelin three-star kaiseki restaurant such as Kanda or Quintessence for a truly unforgettable final evening

day_by_day.notes: teamLab tickets must be purchased online in advance — they frequently sell out weeks ahead. Yanaka is best explored without a strict schedule — allow time to wander. Omotesando Hills and the surrounding streets are excellent for final luxury purchases including Issey Miyake, Comme des Garçons, and premium Japanese pottery.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Japan — enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Depending on departure time, visit the Meiji Jingu Shrine in Harajuku for a peaceful final cultural experience — the forested shrine grounds offer a tranquil contrast to the surrounding city. Purchase final omiyage (souvenir gifts) at the hotel gift shop or a nearby department store basement food hall (depachika).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel and arrange private luxury transfer to Narita or Haneda Airport. Allow at least 3 hours before international departure. Visit the airport's premium departure lounges — Haneda's international terminal has excellent shopping and dining options for final purchases including premium Japanese whisky, matcha confections, and ceramics.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Japan with extraordinary memories of cherry blossoms, ancient temples, world-class cuisine, and unparalleled hospitality. Settle into business or first class for the return journey.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — savor one last full Japanese breakfast with miso soup, grilled salmon, and tamagoyaki
meals.lunch: Premium airport dining at Haneda or Narita — both airports have excellent ramen, sushi, and tempura restaurants in the international terminal
meals.dinner: In-flight dining in business/first class

day_by_day.notes: Depachika (department store basement food halls) at Isetan Shinjuku or Mitsukoshi Ginza are the finest places for omiyage — premium Japanese sweets, pickles, teas, and packaged foods make exceptional gifts. Confirm all luggage weight limits — premium Japanese shopping tends to add significant weight. Keep one carry-on bag accessible for last-minute airport purchases.
